public_rationale: A contemporaneous randomized study found substantially faster completion of professional writing assignments and better assessed output. Its editing analysis also challenges the claim that revision necessarily consumes the drafting advantage. This contradicts the blanket wording when ordinary business copy includes the routine assignments studied. It does not establish that every real publication workflow saves time.
limitations: The evidence concerns short experimental assignments, not complete commercial publishing workflows.
Precise factual accuracy and company-specific requirements were not fully evaluated.
The working paper and published article describe versions of the same experiment, not independent replications.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: ChatGPT can spin up piles of anodyne business copy, but those outputs always require enough editing that it is questionable how much time is actually saved.

statement.excerpt: ChatGPT can spin up piles of anodyne business copy, yet its outputs always require enough editing that it's questionable how much time you've actually saved.

from_speaker: questionable how much time you've actually saved
our_interpretation: The plain reading is that editing routinely consumes enough of the initial drafting advantage to make meaningful overall time savings doubtful, even for ordinary business writing.

Business copy includes routine professional emails, reports, and promotional writing. Controlled assignments resembling this work are relevant, but do not establish performance under every employer's publication requirements.

I use 2023 through the post date as the recent pre-publication observation window for the contemporaneous technology. This capability has no regular reporting quarter; the wording does not limit the observation to work performed on the publication day.
The test concerns total task time and assessed final quality, rather than the speed of generating an initial draft.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous controlled evaluations show that editing and checking generally eliminate substantial time savings on ordinary business-writing tasks at comparable final quality.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous controlled evaluations demonstrate substantial total completion-time savings on ordinary business-writing tasks, including participants' editing, without worse assessed final quality. This would contradict the blanket assertion, without establishing savings for every task.

evidence.publisher: Science; abstract reproduced by Stanford SCALE
evidence.explanation: The randomized experiment involved 453 professionals completing occupation-specific writing assignments. Substantial savings on completed work, accompanied by higher assessed quality, contradict the blanket claim under the stated reading of business copy.

evidence.publisher: Shakked Noy and Whitney Zhang, MIT
evidence.explanation: The original study measured complete assignments and examined editing after generated text was inserted. It reports limited editing and no detected quality advantage from that editing, directly addressing the proposed mechanism that revision consumes the savings.

evidence.locator: Section Simulating work for chatbots, discussion of study limitations
evidence.explanation: The institutional account says the assignments did not require company-specific context or precise factual accuracy, and factual accuracy was not independently checked. Additional production requirements could reduce the measured savings.
